details: This package is a dependency-confusion proof of concept. It ships a sentinel version (99.0.1) under a scoped name with a near-empty tarball, a postinstall hook ("node beacon.cjs"), and an index.js that exports a catch-all Proxy no-op shim so a consumer importing the real package does not crash. On install, and again whenever the module is required, beacon.cjs sends an HTTP POST to hxxp://185[.]158[.]107[.]175:8787/_ah/dc with an X-Beacon-Package header and a JSON body containing only the package name, hostname, install path, working directory and npm user-agent — a callback proving the package was installed. No credentials, environment values, tokens, wallet data or file contents are read or transmitted, and no second-stage payload is fetched. The package's README self-declares it as an authorized dependency-confusion test that only reports installation metadata. This package is a dependency-confusion proof of concept published under a high major version. Its postinstall hook runs beacon.cjs, which sends a single HTTP POST of JSON host metadata — package name, hostname, install path, working directory and Node version — to hxxp://185[.]158[.]107[.]175:8787/_ah/dc with an X-Beacon-Package header. index.js re-fires the same beacon when the module is imported and exports a no-op Proxy so importing code does not crash. No credentials, tokens, environment values or file contents are read or transmitted.
